title: Order checkout failing
executive_summary: INC-007 checkout failures are caused by a configuration change in order-service at 15:22Z that cut payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000ms to 300ms (OPS-2375, config-bot). Order-service error rate jumped from ~0.6% to ~29% and timeout rate from ~0.1% to ~35% starting 15:23Z, with PaymentClient timeouts logged at exactly 300ms. payment-service latency and error rate were flat throughout, so the payment service itself is not degraded, consistent with the payment team's report.

hypotheses.description: order-service payment_client.timeout_ms reduced 3000->300ms, below normal payment call latency tail, causing client-side timeouts, circuit-breaker opening and retry budget exhaustion. Mechanism: At 15:22Z the timeout was set to 300ms. Calls to payment-service POST /v1/charges that exceed 300ms are aborted by order-service, which counts them as failures; the circuit breaker opens (failure ratio 0.64) and retry budget is exhausted, failing checkouts.

probable_root_cause.label: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence)

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): configuration_regression in order-service - order-service payment_client.timeout_ms reduced 3000->300ms, below normal payment call latency tail, causing client-side timeouts, circuit-breaker opening and retry budget exhaustion.
corrective_actions: Revert payment_client.timeout_ms in order-service from 300 back to 3000 (cfg-7f81d14a), and verify error rate returns to ~0.6%
Reset/half-open the payment-service circuit breaker once the timeout is restored and confirm recovery
Replay or reconcile checkouts that failed 15:23Z onward (retry budget exhausted, possible partial charges to check)
preventive_actions: Add CI/config validation with minimum/maximum bounds for timeout values (reject ms-vs-s type ratio changes like 0.1x without approval)
Require review for changes to downstream client timeouts tied to payment paths
Document expected p99 of payment calls and set timeout as a multiple of it
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on order-service PaymentClient timeout rate and circuit breaker OPEN events
Alert on config changes to payment_client.* keys in real time
Track payment-service p99 latency and compare against order-service configured timeout
limitations: Correlation of config change with onset is strong but the mechanism is inferred from timeout logs, not traces
Payment p50/p95 being far below 300ms makes the magnitude of timeouts worth confirming with tail data
[agent-reported gap] payment-service p99 latency not queried
[agent-reported gap] No distributed traces for individual failed checkouts
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The most likely root cause is the config change cfg-7f81d14a in order-service, which lowered payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000ms to 300ms at 15:22Z. Failures begin within a minute, and the logs show timeouts at exactly 300ms. Payment-service health metrics are flat, and DB pool and deployments are not implicated. Residual uncertainty: payment tail latency was not measured directly.
